title: Distinct Subsequences
prompt:
Return the number of distinct ways to choose a subsequence of `s` that equals `t`. Choices differ if they use different index positions.

**Example**: `s = "rabbbit"`, `t = "rabbit"` → `3` (drop any one of the three b's).

**Constraints**: `1 <= s.length, t.length <= 1000`; the answer fits in a 32-bit int.

tests.note: empty t: one way — delete everything

hints: Look at the last character of s. It either helps match the last character of t, or it's skipped. How many ways does each case contribute?
Let dp[i][j] = number of ways the first i characters of s contain the first j characters of t as a subsequence. The empty t is matched exactly one way, so dp[i][0] = 1.
`dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j]` (skip s[i-1]), plus `dp[i-1][j-1]` when `s.charAt(i-1) == t.charAt(j-1)` (use it).

solution.explanation: Each way of matching t[0..j) inside s[0..i) either skips s's last character or uses it to match t's last character, which requires them to be equal. Those cases never overlap, so their counts add. Column 0 counts the single empty match. O(m·n) time and space (O(n) with one row updated right-to-left).
